title: Bone and Tooth Collagen Extraction for Stable Isotope Analysis
author: Prudence Robert
materials: Weight the sample once it is dry.

steps.title: Remove excess water and thaw
steps.instruction: Remove any DI‑water from the tubes containing the bone or dentin samples; if a sample is frozen, allow it to thaw completely and discard the excess DI‑water.

steps.title: Place sample in reaction tube
steps.instruction: Insert the bone or dentin sample into a screw‑cap reaction tube (tube diameter must be 16 mm if an Ezee filter will be used later).

steps.title: Add diluted HCl for demineralisation
steps.instruction: Add approximately 10 mL of diluted HCl to the tube so the sample is fully submerged. Use 0.5 M HCl at room temperature for well‑preserved material; for fragile or highly degraded material use 0.2 M HCl at 4 °C. Do not close the tube tightly because CO₂ will be released. Demineralisation may take longer at lower temperature or lower acid concentration.

steps.title: Replace HCl until demineralised
steps.instruction: Every 2–3 days replace the HCl solution with fresh acid. Observe the tube for bubbling: if no bubbling occurs within 30 minutes at room temperature (or within 01:00:00 if the HCl is stored at 4 °C), consider the sample demineralised. The sample will usually become flexible, transparent and/or float, but lack of bubbling alone is sufficient to deem demineralisation complete.

steps.title: Rinse demineralised sample
steps.instruction: Rinse the demineralised material three times with DI‑water, also rinsing the tube walls. If the sample is fragmented, perform the rinses using an Ezee filter (tube must be 16 mm diameter).

steps.title: Optional short‑term storage
steps.instruction: If the NaOH step will not follow immediately, keep the rinsed sample in the fridge in DI‑water. For crumbly material you may remove the water and store the sample frozen. Store ready samples separately from those still demineralising.

steps.title: Position sample for cutting
steps.instruction: Place the skeletal material on a clean sheet of aluminium foil in a well‑ventilated area.

steps.title: Cut sample to desired mass
steps.instruction: Using a clean mini‑diamond saw mounted on a rotary multifunction tool (e.g., Dremel 3000 or Proxxon), carefully cut a piece of the material of appropriate mass. Keep any bone powder produced on the foil for later analysis.

steps.title: Remove outer surface with drill
steps.instruction: With a clean diamond drill bit, mechanically remove approximately 2 mm of the outer surface of the bone or tooth. Clean the surface with ethanol between each sample and replace the mini‑saw and drill bit with clean ones before the next specimen.

steps.title: Sonicate samples in DI‑water
steps.instruction: Place the cut pieces in a small container, label the container on several sides with the sample ID, add DI‑water, and sonicate for approximately 3 minutes while avoiding any temperature increase. The water may become murky; do not extend the sonication beyond the stated time.

steps.title: Air‑dry overnight
steps.instruction: Leave the container with the samples in a fume hood and allow them to dry overnight.

steps.title: Add 0.25 M NaOH solution
steps.instruction: Add enough 0.25 M NaOH solution to fully cover each sample.

steps.title: Incubate with NaOH and discard
steps.instruction: Let the samples sit in NaOH for 00:15:00 (15 minutes). Discard the NaOH using a Pasteur pipette or an Ezee filter (if the sample consists of small fragments). Space the addition of NaOH for each sample by at least 2 minutes and record the exact start time.

steps.title: Rinse after NaOH treatment
steps.instruction: Rinse the samples and the tube walls three times with DI‑water.

steps.title: Add diluted HCl post‑NaOH
steps.instruction: Add diluted HCl (same concentration as used for the initial demineralisation) so the solution fully covers the samples. This neutralises any CO₂ absorbed by the NaOH and prevents radiocarbon bias.

steps.title: Incubate HCl briefly
steps.instruction: Allow the HCl to react for 00:05:00 (5 minutes).

steps.title: Rinse after HCl step
steps.instruction: Rinse the samples three times with DI‑water.

steps.title: Heat in pH 3 HCl
steps.instruction: Heat the samples in pH 3 HCl solution at 70 °C for 48:00:00 (48 hours) using a programmable oven. Ensure the solution largely covers the samples and add a generous amount to minimise collagen loss.

steps.title: Prepare glass vials and parafilm
steps.instruction: While the samples are heating, label clean glass vials for each specimen, weigh each empty vial, and cut small pieces of parafilm for later covering.

steps.title: Filter solubilised collagen
steps.instruction: When the samples are fully solubilised, slowly press an Ezee filter (tube diameter 16 mm) into each tube to filter the liquid. Transfer the filtered collagen solution into the pre‑weighed glass vials.

steps.title: Freeze vials overnight with parafilm
steps.instruction: Place a cap over the parafilm, then put the glass vials in a freezer overnight.

steps.title: Pierce parafilm and freeze‑dry
steps.instruction: Add a fresh piece of parafilm on top of each vial, pierce it several times with a clean sharp tool (e.g., a toothpick), remove the caps, and place the frozen vials in a freeze‑dryer for at least 24 hours. Transfer the vials quickly between freezer and freeze‑dryer to avoid thawing.

steps.title: Verify complete dryness
steps.instruction: After freeze‑drying, remove the vials and inspect the collagen; it should appear fluffy and white/beige (ice crystals can look similar). Do not thaw partially dried collagen. If dryness is uncertain, continue freeze‑drying (e.g., additional 12 hours), weigh the collagen, and repeat until the mass is constant.

steps.title: Cap vials and weigh collagen
steps.instruction: After removing the parafilm, replace the caps on the glass vials to protect the hygroscopic collagen. Weigh the dry collagen in each vial and calculate the yield; a yield of ≥1 % indicates well‑preserved collagen.

steps.title: Clean saws and drill bits
steps.instruction: Clean all mini‑diamond saws and drill bits by placing them in an ultrasonic bath sequentially in DI‑water, then ethanol, then DI‑water again, repeating each step until the water is clear; each bath lasts 5 minutes.

steps.title: Store dry collagen
steps.instruction: Store the dried collagen in a constantly dry environment, such as a freezer.

steps.title: Repeat rinse‑sonication cycle if needed
steps.instruction: Remove the water from the container, rinse the samples 1–3 times with fresh DI‑water, and add fresh DI‑water. Repeat the sonication step (step 9) until the water in the container remains clear; typically two sonication cycles are sufficient.

steps.title: Recover residual collagen
steps.instruction: After the initial filtration, if collagen solution remains at the bottom of the tube, add additional pH 3 HCl solution and repeat the filtration step (step 19) to maximise collagen recovery.
